extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, supervisory patent classifiers, and other USPTO classification staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO personnel on classifying patent applications and patents, maintaining and creating classes/subclasses, cross-referencing, using classification/search tools, and transferring/assigning applications between art units and Technology Centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use class definitions to determine proper classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions state the subject matter of the classes and subclasses in much more detail than it is possible to state in the brief class and subclass titles. A study of the definitions is essential to determine the proper classification of subject matter within the U.S. Patent Classification System (USPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must study class and subclass definitions (available online) to determine proper classification; definitions give more detail than titles and are essential to correct placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Patent Classification Home Page (Internet & Intranet) resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Classification Home Page is the clearinghouse for classification information published in HTML and PDF, including the Index to the USPC, class definitions, and class schedules; the site integrates with the USPTO Patent Full-Text and Image Database to browse patents in subclasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Classification Home Page (internet and intranet versions) to access index, schedules, and definitions and to link into the Patent Full-Text and Image Database to view patents in subclasses. The intranet site is accessible via the Patent Examiner’s Toolkit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Classification Insight product on the LAN
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification Insight product is a custom browser accessible via the Patent Examiner’s Toolkit containing classification schedules and definitions in PDF and various classification documents in a full-text searchable hyperlinked format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Classification Insight to access Patent Classification Data, U.S. Schedules by class number, class definitions, US-to-IPC concordances, schedules/definitions by Tech Center, and other classification documents (PDFs and searchable text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PCRS for original (OR) and cross-reference (XR) classification information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Classification Retrieval System (PCRS) provides Original (OR) and Cross-Reference (XR) classification information for individual patents and listings of patents contained in subclasses; data updated bimonthly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult PCRS for up-to-date OR and XR classification data, including lists of patents in subclasses and reclassifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Cassis DVD-ROM series for supplemental patent information and search tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Cassis DVD-ROM series provides Patents CLASS (classification lists), Patents BIB (bibliographic info), Patents and Trademarks ASSIGN (assignments), and Patents ASSIST (classification-related files) and full facsimile images (USAPat/USAApp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage Cassis discs for classification lists, bibliographic records, assignment records, and classification manuals; note update frequencies (Patents CLASS/BIB/ASSIGN updated bimonthly; ASSIST every three months) and that DVDs are text-searchable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use automated search tools EAST and WEST (and FPAS) for full-text and classification information
rubrics_metrics.description: EAST and WEST provide examiners with full text of U.S. published applications since 2001, full text of U.S. patents since 1970, optically scanned full text from 1920-1970, current classification information and images for all U.S. published applications and patents; FPAS provides foreign patent documents and English abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EAST/WEST/FPAS for retrieving full-text documents and images, and for current classification info; follow intranet instructions for access and search strategies, and use the Patent Search Room if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Classification Orders for classification changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification orders are issued monthly and detail the changes resulting from classification projects effective that month; used to bridge the gap until manual indices and definitions are updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check monthly classification orders to learn about new or revised class schedules, reassignments of old art, and definition changes that affect searching and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow principles in the Examiner Handbook to the U.S. Patent Classification System
rubrics_metrics.description: Many principles forming the basis of classification are set forth in the Examiner Handbook to the USPC, accessible from the Classification Home Page; questions not covered can be directed to the Office of Patent Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the Examiner Handbook as the foundational guidance for classification decisions and consult the Office of Patent Classification for unresolved issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish new or revised classes/subclasses by following defined steps
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing new classes or revising old ones, the staff performing reclassification should (A) develop an arrangement of documents satisfactory for searching; (B) write/modify the class definition; (C) draw lines between the class and other classes; (D) establish subclass definitions and include them in classification orders; (E) update the Index and Classification Data System files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the enumerated process (A–E) when creating or revising classes/subclasses; publish notification in a classification order and update all relevant systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification orders must include schedules, source/disposition lists, concordances, and definition changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A classification order includes (A) new class schedules or changes to existing schedules; (B) Source and Disposition lists showing how old art was distributed into newly established subclasses; (C) a revised concordance showing relationships to international classification counterparts; (D) necessary changes to definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure classification orders comprehensively document schedule changes, redistribution of art, concordances with IPC, and definition updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Reclassification Alert Report to track recent classification changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reclassification Alert Report is updated quarterly and lists classes and subclasses affected by classification orders issued during the quarter, indicating establishments, abolitions, or definition changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the quarterly Reclassification Alert Report to identify which classes/subclasses have been affected recently and adjust searching/classification accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze the scope of a class by identifying types of subject matter and combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine which types of subject matter (manufacture, art, apparatus, stock material) are in the class and consider combinations such as: basic subject matter combined with an added-purpose feature; combined with a perfecting feature; basic subject matter itself; subcombinations specialized to basic subject matter; and subcombinations of general utility. Examples (stonecrusher) illustrate these types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform an initial analysis to determine the relevant subject matter types and subcombinations, using examples to decide where features fit relative to the class definition; this helps decide proper subclassing or cross-referencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain Technology Center supervisory patent classifier (SPC) assistance when creating new subclasses
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners with approval to create new subclasses should contact the SPC for their technology to receive assistance in transferring patents, determining title and definition of the new subclass, and assigning numeric designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with the SPC before creating subclasses; the SPC will provide instructions and assign designations to make the subclass official and ensure updates to SDF and MCF and automated indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use foreign patent resources (FPAS, STIC) and Translation Branch for foreign documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign patents are available via FPAS, Internet sites, and STIC collections; STIC retains copies and can order photocopies; Translation Branch can assist with language problems in classifying foreign-language patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult FPAS and STIC for foreign patents, forward bibliographic info to SPC for classification updates, and use the Translation Branch when language issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select primary and secondary classifications for patent application publications based on claims and main inventive concept
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary classification is based on the application's main inventive concept using the claims as a guide; there may be any number of secondary classifications for other inventive (mandatory) or valuable disclosure (discretionary) concepts. Applications are classified at least 9 weeks prior to projected publication date, and figure selection for publication occurs at classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the primary classification from the controlling/main inventive concept (claims). Assign secondary classifications for other disclosed inventions or valuable disclosures; ensure timely classification before publication (≥9 weeks) and select figure(s) for publication during classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request addition, deletion, or transfer of classifications using Patent Post Publication Classification Manager tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may use the Patent Post Publication Classification Manager and the PGPub Post Publication Classification Manager to: (A) add any U.S. classification(s) as cross-reference (XR) or secondary classification; (B) delete XR or secondary classifications assigned to the requester's Technology Center; (C) change OR classifications or primary patent publication classification to a classification in the requester's TC; (D) add or delete IPC classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the on-line classification manager tools (available from the Classification Home Page) to request official post-publication classification transactions and follow the specific transaction types (A–D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize harmonized subclasses and their designations
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPC includes subclasses harmonized with EPO and JPO subclasses; these are designated “EPO,” “JPO,” or “EPO/JPO” in parentheses following the subclass title and are regularly populated with EPO/JPO documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying, note harmonized subclass designations and expect populated documents from EPO/JPO databases; treat harmonized subclasses accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner must personally review classification and cross-referencing at allowance and sign IFW form
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is passed to issue, the primary examiner must personally review the original classification and cross-referencing made by assistants in the issuing classification boxes on the IFW issue classification form and provide a full name to show the review was made. An examiner with full signatory authority who acts personally on an application and sends it to issue should stamp and sign only in the 'Primary Examiner' space; draw a line through the 'Assistant Examiner' space if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiners must personally confirm classifications at allowance, sign/stamp appropriately on IFW, and ensure assistants’ entries are clearly indicated or struck-through to avoid oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider every claim separately for classification; mandatory classifications for claims in different classes/subclasses
rubrics_metrics.description: Every claim, independent or dependent, must be considered separately for classification. A separate mandatory classification is required for each claim that is classifiable in a different class or subclass; some claims (e.g., chemical areas) may require plural classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each claim on its own merits for classification. Assign mandatory classifications where a claim falls into a different class/subclass; be prepared to assign multiple classifications for multi-faceted claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine original (OR) classification among mandatory classifications using stated criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: If all mandatory classifications are in the same class, the original classification is the mandatory classification that, looking at the schedule top-down, is the most indented subclass array in which any classifications are assigned (subject to exceptions like genus-species). If mandatory classifications are in different classes, determine OR by, in turn: (A) selection based on the most comprehensive claim; (B) selection based on priority of statutory category of invention; (C) selection based on superiority of types of subject matter; (D) selection among classes in the 'related subject' listing in the front of the manual of classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the listed tie-breaking criteria (A–D) in order to select the OR classification among multiple mandatory classifications, and consult the Examiner Handbook for genus-species and other special rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate remaining mandatory classifications as cross-references and follow alpha/residual/digest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the controlling class is determined, all remaining mandatory classifications are designated as cross-references, as are any additional discretionary classifications. Include alpha subclass designators when appropriate; if a subclass has alpha subclasses and the patent does not fit an indented alpha subclass, include the 'R' (residual) designation. A digest or cross-reference art collection must never be the original classification; digests and cross-reference collections should be put in the cross-reference area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selecting OR, mark other mandatory/discretionary classifications as XRs. Always include correct alpha subclass indicators or 'R' residual, and never select a digest or cross-reference art collection as OR—only as a cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep systematic SEARCH NOTES during prosecution and record consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout examination, systematic notes of cross-references needed (claimed or unclaimed disclosure) should be kept. Each consultation regarding classification or cross-referencing must be recorded in the SEARCH NOTES box on the file wrapper and must include the name of each examiner consulted, the date of consultation, and the results of the consultation including where claimed/unclaimed subject matter is properly classified and whether a cross-reference is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document all classification consultations in SEARCH NOTES with names, dates, and outcomes. Consult examiners handling related subject matter during prosecution to decide on cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cross-references for all claimed disclosure where possible and insert at time of issue
rubrics_metrics.description: A cross-reference MUST be provided for all CLAIMED disclosure where possible and inserted in the issuing classification boxes at time of issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claimed subject matter is cross-referenced when possible and that those XRs are included in the IFW issuing classification boxes before issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for issuing in another Technology Center without transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner issues a prospective patent in another Technology Center (TC), note the class and subclass of the other TC and, in parentheses, the other TC number. A concurring primary examiner from the other TC must initial the area to the right of the original classification. If the primary examiners disagree, submit for resolution to the SPE having jurisdiction; unresolved disputes go to the classification dispute TC representative panel. Only when both examiners concur, or where there has been rulings by SPE or panel, may applications sent to issue from one TC be assigned to classes in another TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow inter-TC concurrence and dispute-resolution steps: record other TC class/subclass and TC number, obtain concurrence signatures, and use SPE/panel resolution if disagreement arises—do not assign across TCs without concurrence or final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Center responsibility and primary examiner authority for assignment and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Technology Center to which an application is assigned is responsible for its examination until officially transferred. Primary examiners have full authority to accept any application submitted to them that they believe is properly classifiable in a class in their art unit. Applicants may be advised of expected transfers using form paragraph 5.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize TC ownership until official transfer; primary examiners can accept applications they deem classifiable in their art unit; use the standard form paragraph to notify applicants of reassignment affecting application location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and assignment of new nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Every nonprovisional application, new or amended (including drawings), when first assigned to a TC must be classified and assigned to an examiner for examination. The supervisory patent examiner normally classifies and assigns the application. Provisional applications are not classified or assigned since they are not examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure nonprovisional applications are classified/assigned promptly (SPC normally does this); do not classify provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT application classification and special situations
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT applications are normally classified on the basis of the first claimed invention (Claim 1). Special situations: (A) if a U.S. national application was acted on by an examiner based on the controlling claim, a subsequent PCT claiming priority will normally be assigned to the same examiner; (B) when U.S. national and corresponding PCT are copending, efforts should ensure both are assigned to the same examiner or art unit; (C) if PCT had international search/examination, the U.S. national phase or national application claiming benefit will be assigned like any other application on the basis of the controlling claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign PCT and related U.S. applications to promote consistent search/examination results, following the listed special-case rules to maintain continuity of examiner assignment when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate inspection of amendments that make transfer proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of an amendment which makes a transfer proper, steps should be taken promptly in accordance with the transfer procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment triggers transfer, promptly follow the transfer procedure (see MPEP § 903.08(d)) to effect the reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer procedures between art units and between Technology Centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers between art units within the same TC follow internal TC procedures. For transfers between different TCs, an SPE believing an application does not belong in his/her art unit may request transfer; applications must be fully reviewed to ensure appropriate areas in the originating TC have been considered; send a transfer inquiry to a receiving art unit; when the receiving SPE agrees, they classify and assign the application and accept the transfer in PALM EXPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the multi-step transfer process: review originating TC coverage, send transfer inquiry, obtain receiving SPE agreement, classify/assign in receiving TC, and accept transfer in PALM EXPO. Prioritize transfers and ensure documentation and notifications (eDAN) are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specific reasons on Application Transfer Request form
rubrics_metrics.description: When effecting transfers, the Application Transfer Request form in PALM EXPO must include a full explanation and at least one of: (A) identification of the controlling claim examinable in another TC; (B) identification of any existing informal transfer agreement; (C) other reasons with full explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear justification on the transfer request form—identify the controlling claim, cite informal agreements, or fully explain other reasons to support the transfer request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gatekeepers/search assistants when unable to determine appropriate receiving art unit
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SPE or examiner believes an application has been improperly assigned but cannot determine where to send it, consult a 'gatekeeper' or search assistant (list available on intranet); gatekeepers exist in all TCs except the TC that examines design applications (TC 2900).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classification/assignment is unclear, consult designated gatekeepers/search assistants to identify the appropriate receiving art unit before requesting transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer on 'best examinable' basis when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application’s claims include a combination of limitations across disciplines, an SPE or primary examiner may request transfer to another discipline on the ground that the application is 'best examinable' in the other discipline, even if controlling claims are properly classified in the original art unit. The requesting SPE/examiner should cite art showing limitations classifiable in the requesting discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-disciplinary applications, consider transfer to the 'best examinable' discipline; support the transfer with art that demonstrates the limitations relevant to the receiving discipline.
